So, my grandfather and his brother aren't plumbers. It turns out that, twenty years ago, they decided to fork the main water line for his house and use the 2nd fork for the garden hose spigot.

Instead of letting the water come all the way in, then branching it back to the spigot so it would have a cutoff valve.. it's an open, unstoppable fork from the main water line that has water all the way through the pipe, to the end. There is no way for me to clear the line of water.

Well, the PVC he used froze over and busted. I went and shut off the water at the street using a wrench and some elbow grease. Then I replaced the parts and the PVC glue is now drying underneath a car floor mat and some old pants holding in heat coming from an electric heater that I ran out to it with a 50ft extension cord.

-

Yes, I do know that it's a flawed design that will fail again. I'll have to dig into the dirt to get to the main line and make any changes which isn't something that I really want to do with snow everywhere, temperatures in the 20s, no prior plumbing experience and being pretty exhausted.

-

My question is:

For right now and until Spring / Summer hits, what can I do to keep the pipe from popping, again?

-

I was considering trying to place a bucket over it with some towels inside.. but I can't get a bucket in between the pipe and the house's foundation. He placed the pipe right next to the foundation bricks. On top of that, he has some weird bracket screwed into the wood of the house to hold the pipe in place so it doesn't get broken by being pulled on when someone runs the garden hose as far as it'll go.

The best idea that I have, now, is to wrap it with some towels and then put a black trash bag over it.

I would be happy to hear some other ideas.
Any ideas on how to keep an outdoor PVC water pipe from freezing?
keep the water running a trickle. It should prevent it from freezing and also if it does freeze it allows room for expansion so your pipes won't crack.

Oh, thanks.. I totally didn't even think of that.

When I go and turn the water back on, in another hour, I'll remember to unscrew it a hair to keep water flowing while its freezing outside.
Heat trace under insulation. Or replace with PEX. It can freeze cock stiff without a problem.

I'd never heard of PEX until now. (Hell, I didn't even know CPVC was a thing until I went to the hardware store, trying to find the PVC parts to fix the current line until it warms up and I can do something better with it.)

I'll look into that. Thank you.
You can put heat tape on it and wrap it with a pool noodle. Trickle water as well.

Thanks.

Currently, I have it wrapped in a thick towel, with a thick black trashbag tightly wrapped around that. I poked a small hole for the nozzle to poke out of and adjusted it so it drips a drop every two seconds.

Yeah, he and his brother just ran a PVC pipe straight out of the main water line with a regular $3 spigot screwed in at the top.

I looked up those frost proof yard spigots. I've seen them, before, but I never knew what they were. I guess I'll have to get him one and get to digging.

Granny told me to just cap that PVC pipe.. but I'm pretty sure that would make the problem worse. At least, right now, I have it slowly dripping. To even remove it, I'd have to dig into frozen ground and try to figure out how he shoddily did what he did.

Real solution is to pull it all up and rebury it so it's below the frost line. If you want to be expedient, look for heat tape that goes inside the pipe.

Other solutions involve training them to drip their faucets when the weather gets cold enough to risk freezing - water's cheap, plumbing's expensive.

Once in the house it travels ~20 feet through the crawlspace and another ~15 feet through the basement, then, right above our water heater, is our first real shutoff valve.. then it runs through the filter and splits in two, with half becoming our cold water and the other half going into the water heater.

I have it working, for now.

Either I'll install one of these at that first splice: https://www.homedepot.com/p/Everbilt-2-ft-Bury-Depth-Frost-Proof-Yard-Hydrant-EBYH02NL/205031731

(I'm leaning towards the first option, as I think the second one may be beyond my abilities.)
